title: Direct & Indirect Speech — Fundamentals, Pronouns & Tense Backshift
description: Direct aur Indirect Speech ke core fundamentals, reporting clause vs reported clause, reporting verbs (say vs tell), pronoun reference shifts (speaker aur listener ke hisaab se), tense backshift matrix, universal truth exceptions, aur contextual time/place adjustments ko master karein.
learningObjectives: Direct Speech aur Indirect Speech ke beech fundamental functional aur syntactic farq ko identify karein
Sentence mein reporting clause, reporting verb, reporting subject, aur reported clause ko accurately isolate karein
Assertive statements ko quotation marks hatakar appropriate conjunction 'that' ke sath Indirect Speech mein convert karein
Reporting verbs 'say', 'tell', aur 'remark' ke syntactic patterns (said that vs told + object) ko correctly apply karein
Speaker, listener (person addressed), aur 3rd person reference ke hisaab se pronouns ko bina meaning distort kiye badlein
Past reporting verb hone par conventional tense-backshift matrix (Present to Past, Simple Past to Past Perfect) ko accurately execute karein
Universal truths, scientific facts, permanent habits, aur present/future reporting verbs mein backshift exceptions ko identify karein
Modal auxiliaries (will to would, can to could, may to might, must to had to) ke backshift rules ko systematically apply karein
Time aur place expressions (today to that day, yesterday to the previous day) ko context-dependent reporting ke hisaab se adjust karein
Rajasthan High Court exams ke common narration traps (told to me, double that, unnecessary backshift, pronoun confusion) ko eliminate karein

included: Direct Speech vs Indirect Speech: definitions, punctuation, quotation marks, and comma conventions
Core narration anatomy: reporting subject, reporting verb, listener/object, and reported speech
Assertive sentence conversions using declarative conjunction 'that'
Reporting verb distinctions: 'said' vs 'said that' vs 'told + object' vs 'remarked'
Pronoun reference shifts: First Person (speaker), Second Person (listener), Third Person (unchanged/referent tracking)
Traditional SON reference guidelines and their semantic limitations
Tense backshift rules with past reporting verbs across all basic tenses and aspects
Modal auxiliary backshift: will/shall to would/should, can to could, may to might, must to had to
Backshift exceptions: Universal truths, established scientific facts, geographical facts, permanent habits, historical facts
Present and future reporting verbs: no backshift when reporting verb is in present (says) or future (will say)
Time and place adverbial shifts: now to then, today to that day, yesterday to the previous day, tomorrow to the next day, here to there, this/these to that/those
excluded: Interrogative sentence conversions: Yes/No questions (if/whether) and Wh- questions with inverted order removal (covered in Lesson 07)
Imperative sentences: commands, orders, requests, advice with 'to + V1' or 'not to + V1' (covered in Lesson 07)
Exclamatory sentences: 'exclaimed with joy/sorrow' and optative wishes/prayers (covered in Lesson 07)
Active and Passive Voice transformations (covered in Lessons 04 & 05)
Conditional clauses and inversions (covered in Lesson 03)
